correctness.rationale: For all 65536 binary 4-by-4 arrays, the exact normalized fourth moment has the autocorrelation identity M=256+2 sum_{24 half-shifts} C^2. An order-eight sign-modulation action is free since a00,a01,a10 uniquely fix its three generators. Actual checker.py exhaustively visits all 8192 normal forms, independently evaluates their moments via coefficients of P^2, and finds minimum 304 with exactly four normal form winners and first greater value 336. Enumerating the full square-dihedral and sign actions gives exactly two disjoint size-16 full orbits covering 32 optima; direct correlation calculations exhibit two magnitude-three shifts, dot-product magnitudes zero or eight, and the common shift-magnitude histogram 16 zeros, six ones, two threes. Exact integer code has been replayed from its actual package path. Finite exhaustive proof only for the stated binary 4x4 domain.

originality.rationale: Known sharp scalar value is expressly excluded from novelty: Schmidt (arXiv:1105.5176, introduction p.2) quotes Eggers 1986 F_4,4=16/3. The claim concerns complete 32-array equality classification into two symmetry orbits, with invariant perpendicular versus oblique large-sidelobe directions. Reviewed accessible full texts study the scalar/asymptotic bound (Schmidt), periodic array families (Svalbe-Tirkel), or complementary array sets (Pai-Chen), not the optimizer classification. Published-record searches found no exact same claim. Full Eggers dissertation and Bomer-Antweiler 1993 text could conceal a matching census: this is a real bibliographic residual risk, not claimed ruled out.

value.rationale: A natural complete finite classification of a fully populated two-dimensional 16-mode binary Fourier aperture, beyond the known scalar optimum. Two geometrically distinct equivalence orbits with identical minimal aggregate aperiodic sidelobe energy but orthogonal versus oblique dominant sidelobes answer a direction-sensitive structural question useful for correlation benchmarks. The exact number 32, two orbit cardinalities, and complete geometry are not mere decimal improvements, renamed parameters, or results implied by the numeric optimum. No unsupported broader engineering performance is claimed.
